operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Fast footage plus kinetic captions". Objective: Repackage existing footage into a clear vertical ad. Visual rule: Each shot has one message; cuts and typography create speed without making the image unreadable. Beats, in order: - 0–1.5 s: Strongest result shot appears immediately with one hook. Shows Brand color, Hero shot, Hook. - 1.5–5 s: Two related shots show the first reason to care. Shows Brand color, Benefit shot 1, Benefit 1. - 5–8.5 s: Switch scene and caption together. Shows Brand color, Benefit shot 2, Benefit 2. - 8.5–12 s: Use the clearest proof/result footage. Shows Brand color, Benefit shot 3, Benefit 3. - 12–15 s: Cleanest hero shot becomes an end card. Shows Brand color, Hero shot, Logo, Call to action and offer. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: hook (Hook: hook, at most 7 words); benefit1 (Benefit 1: benefit 1, at most 7 words); benefit2 (Benefit 2: benefit 2, at most 7 words); benefit3 (Benefit 3: benefit 3, at most 7 words); ctaAndOffer (Call to action and offer: cta, at most 8 words) - images: heroShot (Hero shot: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Strongest result shot appears immediately with one hook. | Cleanest hero shot becomes an end card.); benefitShot1 (Benefit shot 1: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Two related shots show the first reason to care.); benefitShot2 (Benefit shot 2: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Switch scene and caption together.); benefitShot3 (Benefit shot 3: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Use the clearest proof/result footage.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Cleanest hero shot becomes an end card.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
